A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConFu research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original XOR experiments, multimodal retrieval and classification results, and appendix analyses of masking, noise, embedding dimensionality, and few-shot adaptation.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and additionally reports a broader lambda sensitivity comparison and four-modality classification experiments.

M1.justification: The encoder/fusion design and weighted pairwise-plus-fused InfoNCE objective remain unchanged. The arbitrary-modality objective tested in v2 was already defined in v1 Appendix E; its new evaluation does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds a four-modality input scenario by splitting vision into full-resolution grayscale and low-resolution RGB alongside audio and text, evaluated on SSW60 and VB100. All original datasets and tasks, including appendix CUB200 evaluation, are retained; no new data source is evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding existing experiments retain the same CLIP/Tri-CLIP, Symile, GRAM, and TRIANGLE comparators. The new four-modality experiment reuses pairwise CLIP rather than introducing a different comparison method.

E3.justification: The added four-modality experiment introduces grayscale/low-resolution RGB preprocessing and evaluates additional input combinations, including three-input fusion. Previously reported splits, training budgets, metrics, and single-frame/multi-frame bird protocols remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns of those experiments.

E4.justification: New Table 7 expands lambda analysis to accuracy and both retrieval modes at 0.2, 0.5, and 0.8, while retaining the earlier Pareto-selected results as Table 8. Appendix E adds a preliminary test of effectiveness with four modalities. Existing masking, noise, XOR dimensionality, and modality-overlap analyses remain.

E5.justification: New Table 7 supplies standard deviations for aggregate retrieval results previously reported without uncertainty. For example, MUStARD at lambda 0.5 changes from mean-only 45.29/62.56 in v1 Table 7 to 45.3±2.6/62.6±3.1. Existing five-run statements are unchanged; no increase in runs is documented.

E6.justification: Table 2 materially revises aggregate comparisons: UR-FUNNY 1-to-1 ConFu/Tri-CLIP changes from 8.7/6.5 to 7.4/8.1, reversing their reported ranking; MUStARD 2-to-1 ConFu/TRIANGLE changes from 50.0/29.4 to 62.6/50.2. These are corrected averages of unchanged directional scores, not measured performance gains. New Tables 7 and 11 also add sensitivity and four-modality results, substantially expanding the revised result content.

T1.justification: The total-correlation decomposition, InfoNCE bounds, and general subset/retrieval objectives in Appendix E are retained. Equation 6 changes fused-subset notation without changing its mathematics. No new proof, assumption, or derivation accompanies the four-modality experiment.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about unified pairwise/higher-order alignment, Bird-MML, retrieval, classification, and robustness. The four-modality experiment supports an existing generalization claim. The new abstract release statement changes access information rather than the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 newly interprets lambda sensitivity as requiring little tuning and identifies principled lambda selection as future work. Appendix E interprets the artificial four-modality experiment as scalability evidence while acknowledging weak VB100 audio. Section 5.2 removes an explicit inference about avoiding redundant correlations and improving stability across runs.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-dataset release statement with a repository address absent from v1. It also describes construction of the new grayscale/low-resolution RGB inputs. Existing Appendix A architecture, optimization, and preprocessing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 48 works and retain the same research positioning. The added Section 3.3 sentence elaborates the existing contrast between loss-level factorization and joint alignment objectives; reference differences are citation-location changes.

P1.justification: v2 condenses introductory and experimental prose, adds a brief methodological explanation and acknowledgments, corrects author/affiliation text, and converts Section 6 subsection headings to run-in headings. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7 and 11, retaining earlier appendix Tables 7–9 as Tables 8–10. Several figures receive clearer rendering or revised line, grid, legend, and title formatting; figures and tables move within the document. The author block and introductory question display also change, while the two-column design remains.

improvement.justification: Correcting Table 2's inconsistent averages improves the reliability of reported comparisons. The added sensitivity table, aggregate uncertainty estimates, preliminary four-modality evidence, and resource address improve empirical support and reproducibility information. These gains are limited: most results and the method remain unchanged, and Table 11 shows mixed fusion benefits in an artificial scenario, so its broad scalability interpretation warrants restraint.
